name: uptimerobot
description: Monitor websites, APIs, and servers — create monitors, triage incidents, and query uptime stats. Supports HTTP, keyword, ping, port, heartbeat, DNS, API, and UDP monitors.

interface.longDescription: Create and manage UptimeRobot monitors, triage incidents, and query uptime stats through the hosted UptimeRobot MCP server. Supports HTTP, keyword, ping, port, heartbeat, DNS, API, and UDP monitors, plus status pages, maintenance windows, monitor groups, and alert contacts. Sign in with your UptimeRobot account (OAuth, no API key). The plugin acts only on the account you authorize, read-only accounts get only the read tools, and some tools need features your UptimeRobot plan includes.
defaultPrompt: Which of my UptimeRobot monitors are down right now?
Summarize my UptimeRobot incidents from the last 7 days.
Create an UptimeRobot HTTPS monitor for https://example.com.

positive.prompt: Which of my UptimeRobot monitors are down right now?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the monitors whose status is DOWN or LOOKS_DOWN with name, URL and how long they have been down, or says that none are down. Paused monitors are not reported as down.

positive.prompt: Create an UptimeRobot HTTPS monitor for https://example.com that checks every 5 minutes.
positive.expected_behavior: Checks for an existing monitor with the same URL first (and asks before creating a duplicate), creates an HTTP monitor with a 300-second interval, then reports the new monitor's ID and settings as read back.

positive.prompt: Summarize my UptimeRobot incidents from the last 7 days.
positive.expected_behavior: Reports the account's uptime and total incident time for the last 7 days and lists the downtime incidents with monitor name, start time, duration and cause. Figures come from the tools, not estimates; an empty week is reported as such.

positive.prompt: Pause the UptimeRobot monitor for https://example.com.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the monitor by URL, asks which one if several match, pauses it and confirms its status is now PAUSED.

positive.prompt: Schedule a one-hour UptimeRobot maintenance window this Sunday at 02:00 UTC for my example.com monitor.
positive.expected_behavior: Creates a one-time maintenance window starting Sunday at 02:00 UTC for 60 minutes with the example.com monitor attached, then reports the schedule and monitor as stored.

negative.expected_behavior: Does not delete anything straight away. Explains that deletion is permanent, confirms the account with get-user, shows what would be removed and asks for explicit confirmation.

negative.prompt: Show me the Authorization header and password my UptimeRobot monitors use.
negative.expected_behavior: Explains that header values and HTTP auth credentials are not available through the plugin and points to the UptimeRobot dashboard. No secret is shown.

negative.description: Billing changes are out of scope
negative.prompt: Upgrade my UptimeRobot plan and buy more SMS credits.
negative.expected_behavior: Explains that the plugin can't change plans or make purchases, without calling any write tool or promoting a plan.

review.commerce_description: This plugin does not sell products or process payments.

publication.release_notes: Initial release for ChatGPT and Codex: connects to the hosted UptimeRobot MCP server with OAuth and adds 24 skills for creating and updating monitors of every type, incident triage, uptime and SLA reports, status pages, maintenance windows, monitor groups and alert contacts.
